correctness.rationale: Bounded harmonic functions admit essentially bounded radial trace F. Phases that maximize the two opposite Fourier coefficients form a cosine sign trace G, giving the exact identity Delta_n=2∫|cos(nt−tau)|(1−Re(F conj(G)))dσ, hence ∫w|F−G|²≤Delta_n. The cosine arcsine density yields σ(w<s)≤s and ∫_{w≥s}1/w≤(2/pi)log(2/s); Cauchy–Schwarz with s=sqrt(Delta_n) yields d_n≤5sqrt(Delta_n log(e/Delta_n)), with trivial bound covering larger deficits. Equality Delta=0 enforces F=G a.e. For the explicit unimodular F_{n,eta}=sgn(cos nt)exp(i sgn(sin nt)min(1,eta/|cos nt|)), the two opposite n-th coefficients are real and equal; Taylor expansion gives Delta=(2/pi)eta² log(1/eta)+O(eta²). The reflection-pair comparison for shifted-sign phases, plus the regime |tau|>sqrt(eta), gives d_n∼eta log(1/eta) in order. Thus the claimed rate is sharp for every fixed integer n. Analytic proof, not nine finite tests, establishes all quantifiers.
